requirement: Section 7/8: Pass B receives SOURCE + SOURCE CONTEXT + FROZEN INVENTORY, constructs the EXISTING General Covenant IR, and every material composed IR node exposes lineage to one or more inventoryItemIds - additively, without redesigning the IR. Composition may not ignore inventory: every MATERIAL item is REPRESENTED / INTENTIONALLY_NON_COMPUTATIONAL / UNSUPPORTED / AMBIGUOUS, never silently omitted.

additiveIrChanges.lib/contract-model/ir/types.ts: optional `inventoryItemIds?: string[]` on IRExprBase (every expression node), UnlimitedCapacity, IRCondition, IRException, IRRule, IRDefinition, IRSharedCapacity; new optional `IRRule.unresolvedDependencies?: IRUnresolvedDependency[]` (relationshipType, targetRef, description, reason, inventoryItemIds?) - the explicit, never-guessed form of a real cross-unit dependency that normalize.ts previously dropped (populated in commit 4).
additiveIrChanges.lib/contract-model/ir/identity.ts: computeExpressionId/computeCapacityExpressionId exclude inventoryItemIds from the hashed content exactly as they exclude provenance, so attaching lineage never changes an exprId and lineage-free fixtures keep their identities.
additiveIrChanges.nothingElseChanges: no node kind, type rule, validator rule, or enum changed; every new field is optional and absent (not empty) when unused, so pre-existing fixtures/snapshots are byte-identical.

wireChanges.lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic/wir: optional `inventoryItemIds` on WireExpression, WireCondition, WireException, WireRule, WireDefinition, WireSharedCapacity; new `inventoryDispositions: [{inventoryItemId, disposition (tolerant string), note}]` on SubmitCompilationSchema. The submit tool's JSON schema is generated from this Zod schema, so the model sees the new fields automatically.
wireChanges.lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic/nor: withLineage() attaches wire lineage to every normalized rule/definition/shared-cap/condition/exception/expression/UNLIMITED_CAPACITY node (conditional spread - absent when empty); inventoryDispositions pass through verbatim on NormalizedCompilation for Pass C. No interpretation of lineage happens here.

passBInputs.compile.ts: compileCovenantToIR runs resolveSourceContext (anchor = contextBundle.originatingStructuralNodeIds[0]; operativeCharStart from the new optional SemanticCompilerInput.operativeCharStart; documentText from the structural index) and runSemanticInventory BEFORE caller.compile; the caller receives {...input, sourceContext, frozenInventory}.
passBInputs.caller.ts: summarizeAccountability renders, in the first user turn: SOURCE CONTEXT STATE (+ explicit warning when TRUNCATED/STRUCTURALLY_INCOMPLETE), every cross-reference expansion region with provenance, unresolved references, the frozen inventory (one line per item: id, role/materiality/ambiguity, proposition, values, referenced terms/sections, citation + verbatim excerpt), and deterministically-detected values no item covers.
passBInputs.prompt.ts: a SEMANTIC ACCOUNTABILITY block stating the consume-or-disposition obligation, that lineage without value correspondence counts as MISSING, that UNSUPPORTED-consuming-the-item is the safe answer, and that a known-truncated source forbids COMPLETE sufficiency. No financial-term dictionary, no covenant-family dictionary, no benchmark example (the only shared-cap example added in commit 4 is synthetic).

accountabilityRelation: SOURCE COMPONENT -> inventoryItemId (Pass A, verified span) -> IR node inventoryItemIds (Pass B lineage) -> Pass C disposition -> compile failureReasons -> agreement rollup. A definition computation may consume many items (each operand node carries its FORMULA_COMPONENT id); a covenant rule consumes a PERMISSION/PROHIBITION item at rule level, THRESHOLD/VALUE items on literal nodes, CONDITION items on conditions, EXCEPTION items on exceptions, DEPENDENCY/REFERENCE items on dependsOn/unresolvedDependencies, SHARED_CAP items on the WireSharedCapacity.
compileOptions: compileCovenantToIR(input, { caller, cache, inventoryCaller?, accountability? }): inventoryCaller defaults to getStageCaller(); accountability defaults to true. A synthetic inventory caller (no real credential) produces INVENTORY_SKIPPED_NO_PROVIDER - disclosed on result.accountability, never a failure reason - so existing zero-cost orchestration tests keep their meaning while every real run is fully accountable.
versionBump: SEMANTIC_COMPILER_ALGORITHM_VERSION/PROMPT_VERSION -> v4, so no v3-era cached compilation (which carries no accountability) is ever served.
